chapters.title: The Map Is Not the Territory
chapters.sourcePressure: Maps, metrics, statements, plans, and models are useful reductions of reality, but their omissions and makers must be inspected and reality must update them.
chapters.coreMove: Test a representation against ground truth before letting it govern the decision.
chapters.commonMisread: Data and models are bad, so trust anecdotes or instinct instead.

chapters.title: Circle of Competence
chapters.sourcePressure: The model is about knowing the perimeter of earned knowledge; size matters less than knowing where advantage ends.
chapters.coreMove: Mark the edge of earned competence before deciding where to play, learn, or defer.
chapters.commonMisread: Stay comfortable and avoid unfamiliar work.

chapters.title: Falsifiability
chapters.sourcePressure: Popper's standard and Wason's work push claims toward risky tests instead of flexible after-the-fact confirmation.
chapters.coreMove: Turn a claim into a test that could clearly prove it wrong.
chapters.commonMisread: Collect more confirming evidence until the claim feels safe.

chapters.title: First Principles Thinking
chapters.sourcePressure: The source contrasts inherited analogy with breaking a problem down into fundamental truths, using Lego disassembly, Socratic questioning, Five Whys, and Musk's battery and SpaceX examples.
chapters.coreMove: Strip inherited assumptions from a problem and rebuild from what is actually true.
chapters.commonMisread: Be more innovative by ignoring tradition.

chapters.title: Thought Experiment
chapters.sourcePressure: Thought experiments are structured mental simulations that simplify reality to test implications when physical experimentation is impossible, costly, or premature.
chapters.coreMove: Run a constrained mental simulation to expose hidden assumptions before reality charges the full price.
chapters.commonMisread: Imagine freely and call any scenario a thought experiment.

chapters.title: Necessity and Sufficiency
chapters.sourcePressure: Frozen support is thin; keep to the distinction between conditions that must be present and conditions that are enough to produce the outcome.
chapters.coreMove: Separate must-have conditions from enough-to-produce conditions before choosing the lever.
chapters.commonMisread: List every helpful factor and treat them all as equally required.

chapters.title: Second-Order Thinking
chapters.sourcePressure: The official framing asks the reader to trace consequence chains past the immediate result with the practical question, And then what?
chapters.coreMove: Trace what the first result will cause next before choosing the attractive move.

chapters.title: Probabilistic Thinking
chapters.sourcePressure: The model asks the reader to replace certainty with likelihoods, multiple possible futures, Bayesian updating, fat-tailed curves, and asymmetries.
chapters.coreMove: Hold several possible futures with weighted odds and act where the payoff and downside are asymmetric.
chapters.commonMisread: Say anything could happen and avoid commitment.

chapters.title: Causation vs. Correlation
chapters.sourcePressure: Frozen support is thin; keep to the practical warning that things moving together do not prove one produced the other.
chapters.coreMove: Demand a plausible mechanism or test before treating association as cause.
chapters.commonMisread: Correlation is worthless and should always be ignored.

chapters.title: Inversion
chapters.sourcePressure: The source frames inversion as solving backward: ask what would cause failure, error, or ruin, then remove those causes.
chapters.coreMove: Work backward from failure and remove the causes before chasing success directly.

chapters.title: Occam's Razor
chapters.sourcePressure: Frozen support is moderate and narrow; prefer the simpler sufficient explanation or structure, while stating that simplicity is not proof.
chapters.coreMove: Choose the simplest sufficient explanation first, then add complexity only when the evidence forces it.
chapters.commonMisread: The simplest story is always true.

chapters.title: Hanlon's Razor
chapters.sourcePressure: Frozen support is moderate and narrow; do not rush to malice when ordinary error, ignorance, or confusion may explain enough, but do not deny real malice.
chapters.coreMove: Check ordinary error before assigning hostile intent, while preserving the evidence that would change the call.
chapters.commonMisread: Excuse harmful behavior and never hold anyone accountable.
